chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Dry dates are not valid [to be exchanged] for fresh dates because the dry one is dry and the fresh one is moist; so when the fresh one dries out, it decreases [in volume/weight]."
He said: "And barley is not valid [to be exchanged] for wheat except one for one."
And he said: "The measure [by volume] runs in a single manner."
He said: "And it is disliked [to exchange] a qafiz of almonds for two qafizs, and a qafiz of dates for two qafizs."
But [it is valid] a sa' of wheat for two sa's of dates, and a sa' of dates for two sa's of raisins.
When this [difference in density/moisture] varies, and dried fruit runs in a single manner [i.e., equal exchange is valid].
He said: "There is no objection to exchanging merchandise as long as it is not by measure or by weight."

key_terms.صَاعٌ: A specific unit of volume measurement
key_terms.قَفِيزُ: A specific unit of volume measurement

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for exchanging dates and grains in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the application of *riba al-fadl* by distinguishing between homogeneous goods, which require equal measure to prevent hidden defects (*gharar*) from moisture loss, and heterogeneous goods, which permit unequal ratios like one measure of wheat for two of dates. It further refines commercial jurisprudence by permitting the exchange of general merchandise (*muta'*) without strict measurement, provided the items are not inherently measured or weighed commodities.
